newsitem.title: UK: London precious metals pop higher on shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: London precious metals pop higher on shortcovering.

text.p: Precious metals prices took a tentative stab at the upside on Tuesday afternoon, with gold posting short covering gains of about $1.50 an ounce.
Gold remained at 18-month lows after drifting lower overnight and in early Europe, depressed by U.S. dollar strength and the absence of physical and investor demand.
But it fixed firmer at $378.65 an ounce following a midday short covering rally, compared to $377.05 in the morning and Monday's London finish of $378.35/$378.85.
Silver also firmed following news of lower than expected silver stocks at Wilmington Trust, dealers said.
According to traders in New York, Comex said that Wilmington had 59.4 million ounces of silver on Sept 30.
Analysts had estimated Wilmington, which becomes an official exchange silver depository from Jan 1, 1997, could have up to 100 million ounces.
"It's had a good little rally. Gold was following to some extent but there's also been some short covering there," a London-based dealer said.
Silver was indicated at $4.92/$4.96, up six cents from Monday's close. Its upside target was the key $5.00, although analysts said it would meet layers of resistance on the way up.
Dealers and analysts were mixed as to whether gold and silver would resume probing the downside following the shortcovering bounce.
"I think we've seen the bottom. The market's incredibly short, it's going to have to go higher," one dealer said.
But analysts warned that, having breached key support levels in recent days, the upside would be a struggle for both metals despite being oversold.
"The market took out major support at $380 and $378.40, and although it is oversold it will be difficult to pull back," analyst Karen Jones of Credit Suisse said of gold.
Bids for gold were quoted so far between $379.00 and $376.90, while silver bids were between $4.94 and $4.83.
Platinum firmed with the others after sliding to a new near two-year low fixing in the morning of $381.50 an ounce.
It was indicated at $383.75/$384.75, on par with Monday's London close after hitting a low bid of $380.50 early on.
"Platinum's recovered quite well. It's following the whole complex as it has been," a dealer said. Platinum was expected to run into resistance around $385, with support at $380.
Palladium was $0.75 firmer at $119.00/$120.00. --Lida Poletz, London newsroom =44 171 542 2936
